character: 4.048-mile (6.52km) fast, flowing Wisconsin road course with minimal barriers and huge braking zones after long straights. Momentum through the sweepers and a strong exit from Canada Corner onto the front straight define lap time.

corners.name: Turn 1
corners.type: heavy-braking right-hander after the front straight
corners.technique: Brake hard from top speed, late apex to set up the run to Turn 3
corners.trap: Over-braking and giving up momentum into the following section

corners.name: Turn 5
corners.technique: Commit with smooth steering, carry speed into the following sequence
corners.trap: Lifting unnecessarily kills momentum through the fast section

corners.name: Kink
corners.technique: Minimal steering input, trust the car at speed
corners.trap: Any correction at this speed is highly costly — regarded as the track's most demanding corner

corners.name: Canada Corner
corners.type: heavy-braking hairpin after a long downhill run
corners.technique: Brake hard and late, patient throttle on exit
corners.trap: Locking up on the long downhill approach

corners.name: Turn 14
corners.type: final corner onto the front straight
corners.technique: Late apex, clean exit is critical — feeds the front straight
corners.trap: Compromised exit costs time down the entire straight
